features.title: Why {brand} stays up when others go down

ech.title: Your connection is invisible
ech.description: Encrypted Client Hello hides the server name from anyone watching the wire. There is no fingerprint to block.

k2cc.title: Full speed on broken networks
k2cc.description: k2cc tells interference apart from real congestion and keeps sending. On a 26% loss link it delivers 2–5× the throughput of BBR.

transport.title: Switches routes before you notice
transport.description: QUIC first, TCP-WebSocket when QUIC is blocked. The switch happens mid-session, without dropping what you were doing.

privacy.title: No logs, and you can check
privacy.description: We don't record what you do. The protocol is documented, the server is open source, and you can run your own k2s node and use {brand} only as a client.

pricing.title: One plan. Every device.
pricing.subtitle: Five devices, unlimited data, every location. Cancel any time.

whatIsK2.question: What is k2?
whatIsK2.answer: k2 is the tunnel protocol behind {brand}. It combines Encrypted Client Hello, a QUIC and TCP-WebSocket dual transport, and the k2cc rate controller. The protocol is documented on this site under /k2, and the server (k2s) is open source.

lossySpeed.question: Why does it stay fast when my network drops packets?
lossySpeed.answer: Most VPNs slow down as soon as packets go missing, because their congestion control assumes loss means congestion. k2cc measures the link instead, tells interference apart from real congestion, and keeps the rate up. In our tests at 26% packet loss it delivers 2–5× the throughput of BBR.

ech.question: What does ECH do for me?
ech.answer: Encrypted Client Hello encrypts the part of the TLS handshake that normally reveals which server you are connecting to. An observer sees an ordinary HTTPS session to a public site and nothing else.

platforms.question: Which platforms are supported?
platforms.answer: Windows, macOS, iOS and Android. One subscription covers five devices at the same time.

logs.question: Do you keep logs?
logs.answer: No. We do not record the sites you visit or the traffic you send. We keep only what a subscription needs: your email, the plan you bought, and the devices signed in.

selfHost.question: Can I run my own server?
selfHost.answer: Yes. k2s is open source and installs with one command. Add your own node in the app and {brand} becomes just the client.

pricing.question: How much does it cost?
pricing.answer: $79 per year, or $8.99 per month on a 12-month term. Both include five devices, unlimited data and every location. Prices are in US dollars; your card is charged in your own currency.

payment.question: How can I pay?
payment.answer: Credit or debit card through Stripe. Apple Pay and Google Pay are offered at checkout where your device supports them.

devices.question: How many devices can I use?
devices.answer: Five at the same time, on any mix of platforms. Signing in on a sixth device signs out the oldest one.

wifiSwitch.question: What happens when I switch from Wi-Fi to mobile data?
wifiSwitch.answer: The tunnel migrates with you. QUIC carries the session across the network change, so downloads and calls continue without reconnecting.

cancel.question: How do I cancel?
cancel.answer: From your account page, or through the app store you subscribed with. Your plan stays active until the end of the period you paid for.
